claims.claim: Linezolid, a close oxazolidinone analog sharing the same 2-oxazolidinone core and N-aryl substitution, has almost 100% oral bioavailability in fasted healthy volunteers; this is the most transferable direct F evidence for the query under fasted conditions.
GSK1322322 absolute oral bioavailability was 57% in the fasted state in healthy volunteers, above the 20% threshold.
Suvorexant absolute oral bioavailability was 82% under fasted conditions, above the 20% threshold.

Additional L1 records report F values above 20% or good oral bioavailability (zalcitabine 80%, asciminib ~73%, elinzanetant 36.7%, cladribine 36-46%, venadaparib good, GSK1322322 fed 77%), providing consistent supportive direction despite lower structural transferability.
The only threshold-level record, lurasidone 20%, was measured in the fed state and is structurally unrelated; it does not provide affirmative fasted-state evidence against the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental F measurement exists for the query molecule itself.

Structural differences from linezolid (5-chlorothiophene carboxamide, morpholin-3-one instead of morpholine, higher molecular weight/logD) could alter absorption or first-pass, but no affirmative evidence indicates F < 20%.
L2 records are not yet available; additional context could refine confidence.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high: the query is a close fasted-state oxazolidinone analog of linezolid (F ~100%), and all transferable fasted-state absolute bioavailability records are above 20%; no affirmative evidence supports F < 20%.
